sourceMathEvidence: Current stem gives two quadratics with f(x)≤0≤g(x), the exact center range k∈[−1,2] for equal interval extrema on [k−3,k+3], and the common tangent line y=−2x. It asks f(2)+g(2); choice ① is −9/2.
solutionMathEvidence: Because the extrema equality forces both interval extrema to be zero, the k-range determines the unordered vertex abscissae {−1,2}. Testing the swapped assignment against y=−2x gives intersection discriminants 16u+4>0 and 8v+4>0, so it cannot be tangent. With f=−u(x+1)² and g=v(x−2)², D=0 gives u=1/2 and v=1/4. Then f(2)=−9/2, g(2)=0, sum=−9/2, matching choice ①.
